caseno: Criminal Appeal No. 2236 of 1993 with Criminal Appeal No. 2289 of 1993.
lawyer:
ANM Gaziul Haque with Kani Lal Saha, Advocates  --- For the Appellants.  
No One --- For the State.
parties:
Nuruddin Ahmed (Md) and 2 others ------ Appellant
Vs.
State ------ Respondent
full_judgment:
These two appeals are directed against the judgment and order dated 14-11-93 passed by the Divisional Special Judge, Rajshahi Division, Rajshahi in Special Code No.4 of 1993 (Bogra), which arose out of Begra PS Case No.14 dated 27-2-88 and GH Case No.4 of 1988, convicting accused appellants Md. Nuruddin Ahmed, Md Hamidul Haque and Md Mahfuzur Rahman of Criminal Appeal No.2236 of 1993 under sections 468/109 of the Penal Code and sentencing them thereunder to suffer RI for two years and to pay a fine of Taka 2000.00 each, in default, to suffer RI for further period of three months while convicting co-accused Moyezuddin Akand of Criminal Appeal No.2289 of 1993 under section 468 of the Penal Code and sentencing him thereunder to suffer RI for two years and to pay a fine of Taka 1000.00, in default, to suffer RI for a further period of 3 months and further convicting him under section 471 of the Penal Code and sentencing him thereunder to suffer RI for six months and to pay a fine of Taka 1000.00 in default, to suffer RI for a further period of one month. The sentences passed against the appellants were to run concurrently.

2. The prosecution case, in short, is that, on the basis of a complaint from the Upazila Magistrate, Sadar Bogra to the effect that the Balam Register of the Sub-Registrar office of Bogra for the year 1932 was tampered and forgery was committed there in pursuance of which an inquiry was held by the Bureau of Anti-Corruption. On completion of the inquiry, its report, Ext. 1, was filed and Assistant Inspector Nazrul Islam attached to the District Anti-Corruption Bureau Bogra was given the responsibility to further enquire into the matter whereupon it transpired that 6.53 acres of land in lot No.107 of Mauza Sona Kandi was sold by Syed Ali Akand and Hazrat Ali Akand to one Ishaque Ali Khalifa of Brindabanpur of Bogra town by a registered deed of sale bearing No.2859 dated 12-7-1993 and the said land was subsequently recorded in the names of the said lshaque Ali and his sons. Subsequently, the C & B Division acquired 4.16 acres of land out of the aforesaid 6.53 acres of land for temporarily supplying sands for manufacturing brick for the construction of a public road on payment of compensation for crops. Subsequently, Ishaque Ali Akanda gifted the said land of his two wives by a registered deed of gift. In course of time the wives and sons of Ishaque Ali sold the said land to PW Md Nazrul Islam by different kabalas and since then he possesses the same. Accused Mayezuddin in collusian with other persons attached to the Sub-Registrar's office, Sadar Bogra fraudulently caused disappearance of the certificate of the Sub-Registrar in Volume IX of the year 1993 and fraudulently purported to create a false deed of gift in the said volume bearing No.672 covering pages 53-55 of the volume in question, showing gift of land vide deed No. 672 dated 29-6-32 in respect of the land of plot No.107 of Mouza Satkania showing accused Md Moyezuddin Akanda as the recipient of the deed of gift and Syed Ali Akand and Hazrat Ali Akand as the executants. It has been alleged that the creation of the said document exposes the evil ingenuity of the accused persons in destroying public documents. The aforesaid deed of gift is evidently fraudulent and collusive and the relevant entry in the volume is also false and fraudulent. As spurious documents the said two documents do not contain any certificate of the Sub-Registrar and these have been written with fountain pen while the preceding documents were all written with country made ink made of leaves of trees and these had no similarities with other documents contained in the said volume. Accused Hamidul Haque wrote those false documents in the volume book while accused Mahfuzur Rahman passed order for supplying certified copy of the disputed forged deeds, although the same were not entered in the corresponding Index book. Accused Nuruddin assessed the copy of the certified copy of the forged deeds while accused Aminur Rahman got the certified copy of the said forged deeds of gift authenticated. Accused Moyezuddin Akanda on obtaining the certified copy of the said forged deeds of gift filed Title Suit No. 93 of 1986 in the Court of the Subordinate Judge, Bogra for declaration of his title in that suit land and hence the case.

3. An officer of the Bureau of Anti-Corruption held investigation of the case, examined witnesses and recorded their statements under section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, seized alamats and on completion of the investigation submitted charge sheet against the accused persons under sections 420/467/468/471/105 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of Act II of 1947.

4. Upon the aforesaid allegations 5 accused persons were put on trial before the Divisional Special Judge, Rajshahi Division, Rajshahi in Special Case No. 4/93 to answer charges under sections 420/467/468/471/105 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of Act II of 1947 to which they pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.

5. At the trial the prosecution examined two witnesses in support of its case and the accused examined none. The learned Divisional Special Judge, by his impugned judgment dated 14-11-93 convicted accused appellant Moyezuddin Akanda under section 468 of the Penal Code and sentenced him to suffer RI for 2 years and to pay a fine of Taka 1000.00, in default, to suffer RI for a further period of three months and further convicted him under section 471 of the Penal Code and sentenced him to suffer RI for a further period of six months and to pay a fine of Taka 1000.00, in default, to suffer RI for a further period of one month while convicting accused Nuruddin, Hamidul Haque and Mafizur Rahman under sections 468/109 of the Penal Code and sentenced them thereunder to suffer RI for two years and to pay a fine of Taka 2000.00, in default, to suffer RI for a further period of three months and acquitted co-accused Aminur Rahman of the charges leveled against him. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid order of conviction and sentence, the accused appellants preferred these appeals.

6. Mr Gaziul Haque, the learned Advocate appearing for the appellants, submits that the learned Divisional Special Judge was wrong in convicting the accused appellants mostly on surmises and conjectures and not on the basis of the evidence on record and, as such, the impugned order of conviction and sentence is not maintainable in law. The learned Advocate further submits that the learned Divisional Special Judge has failed to consider the case of the individual accused persons in the light of the evidence on record and consequently fell in error in generalizing the guilt of the accused appellants and the same has occasioned failure of justice. Mr Gaziul Haque further submits that in view of the admitted fact that accused Moyezuddin Akanda used the disputed deed of gift Ext. 8 in Title Suit No.93 of 1986 before the Subordinate Judge, Bogra. No Court can take cognizance of the alleged offence without any complaint from that Court and, as such, the present criminal proceeding is barred under section 195(1)(c) of the Code of Criminal Procedure and consequently the impugned order of conviction and sentence is not sustainable in law.

7. Mr Khandaker Mahbub Alam, the learned Assistant Attorney General appearing for the State, on the other hand, submits that the learned Divisional Special Judge on detailed discussion and proper appreciation of the evidence on record was perfectly justified in convicting and sentencing the accused-appellants on the basis of most cogent and convincing evidence and, as such, the impugned judgment does not call for any interferences by this Court. The learned Assistant Attorney General further submits that the bar to prosecution as envisaged by section 195(1)(c) of the Code of Criminal Procedure has reference only to a forged deed and not a copy of it and, as such, the protection afforded by section 195(1)(c) of the Code of Criminal Procedure is not available to the accused appellants and consequently, the submissions made by the learned Advocate for the appellants are of no substance. Point for determination

8. The only point for determination in the appeal is whether the learned Divisional Special Judge was justified in passing the impugned order of conviction and sentence.

Findings and decision

9. Mr Gaziul Huque has placed before me the impugned judgment as well as the evidence of the witnesses examined by the prosecution. To appreciate the submissions made by the contending parties it is necessary to scrutinize the material evidence on record.

10. In this case the FIR was lodged by Assistant Inspector Md Nazrul Islam attached to the Bureau of Anti-Corruption, Bogra. This FIR has been marked as Ext. 15.

11. PW 1 Md Nazrul Islam, who was an Assistant Inspector attached to the Bureau of Anti-Corruption, Bogra in 1986, stated in his evidence that the case was referred to the District Bureau of Anti-Corruption from the Court of the Upzila Magistrate, Bogra for inquiry. Thereafter, it was endorsed to him for holding enquiry by E/R/No. 103/86. He stated that in the course of the enquiry he seized alamats from the office of the Sadar Sub-Registry Office, Bogra, the Thumb Impressions Register and Volume No. II of the year 1932 under proper seized list. He also seized the search application dated 19-10-85. These have been marked as Exts 2, 3, 4 and 5 respectively. He seized other papers under proper seizure lists under Exts 6 & 7. He also seizure the certified copy of the disputed deed of gift bearing No. 672 dated 23-7-87 under a proper seizure list. This disputed deed of gift has been marked as Ext 8. He also stated that he also seized sale deed No. 2359 dated 12-7-32 marked Ext. 9 and sale deed No. 13516 marked Ext. 9 Ka. He also seized the Index Register of Volume No. II from the Sadar Sub-Registrar's Office, Bogra for the year 1932 marked Ext 10 (beginning from No. 149). He also seized the Index of Volume No. 4 of the said office for the year 1932 marked Ext. 11 and the Index of Volume No. 3 for the year 1932 marked Ext. 12 and the Index of Volume No. 1 for the year 1932 marked Ext. 13, the application for supply of the copy of the disputed deed of gift vide seizure list Ext. 2 (Gha). He further stated Syed Ali Akanda and Hamid Ali Akanda sold 4.47 acres of land in plot No. 107 of Mouza 'Sonakania' along with other land to Md Ishaque Ali Khan by a registered sale deed bearing No. 2859 dated 12-7-1933. This land was subsequently acquired by the C & B in the year 1971 for the purpose of manufacturing brick vide LA Case No. 4/G/71 on payment of compensation to its owner Md Ishaque Ali and his Bargadars. He further stated that subsequently, Ishaque Ali made a gift of this land in favour of his two wives. Thereafter, the wives and sons of Ishaque Ali sold the said land to one Nazrul Islam and others by registered sale deeds. He further stated that accused Md Moyzuddin, in collusion with other accused persons, created a false deed of gift bearing No. 672 purportedly showing his father Syed Ali Akanda and uncle Hamid Ali Akanda as the executants of the said deed in Volume No. XX of 1932. He stated that accused Mahfuzur Rahman filed an application for the certified copy of the aforesaid false deed on 19-10-85 although it was never entered in the relevant Index Register while accused Nuruddin, record keeper of the Sub-Registrar's Office, assessed the cost of the certified copy of that false deed. He also stated that accused Habibur Rahman Khan got the disputed certified copy authenticated. He stated that on obtaining the certified copy of the false deed in question accused Moyzuddin filed Title Suit No. 93 of 1986 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, Bogra claiming the case property.

12. In cross-examination he stated that he went to the office of the Sub-Registrar after the case was endorsed to him. He admitted that he cannot say when accused Nurul Islam took charge of the record room. He denied the defence suggestion that accused Moyezuddin Akanda got his name mutated in respect of the case land on the basis of the disputed certified copy. He also stated that there is no interpolation or erasure at Nos. 53-57 of Volume No. 1. He further stated that on receiving the hand writing expert's reports he filed the FIR. He stated that volume Ext. 6 does not contain the official seal but it contains the signatures of Sub-Registrar on the right hand side.

13. In reply to the defence question he stated that enquiry was held on the complaint of PW 2 Md Nazrul Islam. He further stated that the disputed false deed has been entered in Nos. 53-57 of Volume No. 11 of the year 1932 and there is no mark of erasure or interpolation therein. He denied the defence suggestion that Nos. 51-52 were not torn when he seized the volume in question.

14. In reply to the suggestion of the accused, he also stated that accused Moyzuddin was a bargadar under Ishaque Ali in respect of the case land. He also stated that PW 2 Nazrul Islam purchased the case land in 1985 and troubles started after his purchase. He stated that he could not examine Syed Ali Akanda, Hamid Ali Akanda, the executants of sale deed; as they were already dead. This disputed deed of gift was in respect of six acres of land. He stated that he did not know if Title Suit No. 93 of 1986 ended in any compromise.

15. PW 2 Nazrul Islam stated in his evidence that Syed Ali Akanda, Hazrat Ali Akanda and Asgar Ali Akanda were three full brothers. Asgar Ali died leaving a son and wife. Syed Ali and Hazrat Ali sold 4.73 acres of land along with other lands to Reazuddin Khalifa in 1932 and Reazuddin Khalifa used to possess this land through bargardar accused Moyzuddin. He further stated that Reazuddin, Habib and Mojibor used to barga cultivate the case land. He stated that the C&B acquired this land during the year 1971 for the purpose of manufacturing brick and compensation was paid to its owner Reazuddin and his bargardars as compensation for crops. He also stated that a khatian was subsequently prepared in the name of Reazuddin. Eventually, Reazuddin gifted in 1975 this land by a registered heba-bil-ewaz deed in favour of his two wives Aimona and Belayetunnessa. He also stated that in the year 1984 he purchased 2.63 acres of land in case plot No. 107 from the three sons of Aimona and Belayetunnessa while Abul Hossain Akanda purchased the remaining portion of 2 other sons. He aslo stated that he purchased 33 decimals of land from Abul Hossain while bargadar Habibur Rahman purchased some land from Aiman Nessa after they went into possession of the case land. He went on to state that Moyzuddin started creating troubles and threatened to forcibly take away paddy from the case land following which a salish was held and the village elders forbade him to forcibly take away paddy from the case land when accused Moyzuddin threatened to file a pre-emption case against him if he was not given the land in Bogra. He stated that 15 days thereafter Moyzuddin gave out that he had interest in the case land and produced a photo copy of a deed before the salish but subsequently he took it away. Thereafter on the advice of the salisadars he enquired about the matter in the local Sub-Registrar''''s Office. Subsequently, it transpired that accused Moyzuddin had filed a suit in the civil Court for correction of the records of rights. On enquiry, it was found that there was no index of the disputed deed of gift bearing No. 672, following which he filed the case in the Court of the local Magistrate. This petition of complaint has been marked as Ext. 16.

16. In cross-examination he stated that from the Court of the Subordinate Judge, Bogra he learnt about the disputed deed of gift and thereafter he went to the office of the Sub-Registrar to examine the relevant volume. He denied the defence suggestion that he had created false papers in proof of his possession in respect of the case land against the accused. He also stated that after purchasing the case land he got his name mutated and paid rent in his own name to the appropriate authority. He refuted the defence suggestion that Syed Ali Akanda and Hazrat Ali Akanda rightly gifted 6 acres of the case land to accused Moizuddin by a registered deed of gift in the year 1932. He further stated that he became defendant in Title Suit No. 93 of 1986 filed by accused Moyzuddin and the said suit was eventually compromised whereby accused Moyzuddin disowned his claim in the suit land.

17. From a close scrutiny of the evidence of the witnesses discussed above it is evident that the disputed deed of gift Ext. 8 was entered in Volume No. 11 of 1932 of the office of the Sub-Registrar, Bogra fraudulently and collusively. It also appears from Ext. 4 in Volume No. 11 of the year 1932 of the office of the Sub-Registrar that deed No. 672 was the last deed in the said volume after which the Sub-Registrar duly endorsed the completion certificate of the volume but the completion certificate was subsequently torn and taken away by the accused persons for making room for accommodating two more spurious entries in the said volume in respect of the disputed deed of gift No. 672 and another fictitious deed bearing No. 673. It also appears from Ext. 4 and Ext. 8 that the disputed deed of gift No. 672 and subsequent deed No. 673 in the said volume No. II were not written in the country-made ink as was done in case of the preceding deed. Ext. 8 does not also contain the certificate of the Sub-Registrar and other necessary endorsements. It has been proved by both documentary and oral evidence that accused Hamidul Huq is the writer of the disputed Heba-bil-ewaz deed, the writings of which are in his own hand. It is manifestly evident from Ext. 9 sale deed No. 2359 dated 12-7-1992 that Syed Ali Akanda and Hazrat Ali Akanda sold 6.53 acres of land to Ishaque Khalifa and this deed is the last deed entered in volume No. 11 of 1932, after which the Sub-Registrar duly made an endorsement of the completion of the said volume. It is evident from Ext. 4 that the disputed deed of gift appearing in Volume No. 11 of 1932 has been created in the name of accused Md Syed Ali Akanda and Hazrat Ali Akanda as its executants. This deed of gift has been marked as Ext. 8. It also appears that all the preceding documents contain the signatures of the Sub-Registrar at the specified places but the disputed deed of gift No. 672 does not contain any such signature. There is no earthly reason why it does not contain the signature of the Sub-Registrar concerned. It also appears that the accused persons in collusion with each other have deliberately caused disappearance of the endorsement of the Sub-Registrar signifying the completion of the volume in question for accommodating the two forged and fabricated documents. It is also seen from Ext. 4 that it does not contain any completion certificate of the Sub-Registrar and blank space after deed No. 673 remains unused. It is found from Ext. 9, the Index Register for the relevant period, that there is no indexing of the disputed deed of gift therein which is a natural corollary of a genuine document. From Ext 11, 12 and 13, the Index Registers for the period in question, it is manifestly clear that the disputed deed of gift was never entered in the Index Register and there no explanation for this. On entry of the disputed civil of gift No. 672 Ext. 4 in the relevant register clearly proves that the alleged deed of gift was not in existence in the year 1962 but it was subsequently manufactured for making illegal gains. It is also evident that Ext. 4 has been subsequently manufactured for laying a false claim in the case land by accused Moyzuddin Akand.

18. The learned Divisional Special Judge on consideration of the material evidence, both oral and documentary, found that the disputed deed of gift Ext 4 was created by accused Md Moyezuddin for depriving PW 2 Md Nazrul Islam of his valuable land by resorting to forgery. The learned Judge further found that at the time of creation of the alleged deed of gift Ext. 4 accused Moizuddin was only 9 years old and, as such, there cannot by any question of making a gift of the case property to him in lieu of his service rendered to the cause of the executants.

19. To ascertain the fact as to who was the author of Ext. 4, standard signatures and standard writings of accused Hamidul Haque appearing in volume No. 380/1984 Ext. 6 Ka from No. 192-238 were sent to the hand writing expert for his comparison and opinion and the hand writing expert opined that accused Hamidul Haque is the writer of the disputed deed of gift Ext. 4. The report of the hand writing expert has been marked as Ext. 18 without any objection. It is thus manifestly clear that accused Hamidul Haque entered this disputed deed of gift Ext. 4 in volume No. 11 of the year 1932 of the office of the Sub-Registrar, Bogra knowing it full well that the alleged  deed of gift was a false and fabricated one.

20. The allegation against accused Nurul Islam is that he was the Record Keeper of the Sub-Registrar's office Bogra and he made assessment for the certified copy of the disputed deed of gift Ext. 4, although page No. 2 of the said volume was torn. It is also alleged that he filed an application for the certified copy of the disputed deed of gift marked Ext. 4. Accused Aminur Rahman simply got the certified copy of the disputed deed of gift verified. From Ext 14 it is found that the accused Mahfuzur Rahman filed an application for the certified copy of the disputed deed of gift. Since there was no indexing of the disputed deed of gift Ext. 4 there was no entry in any Index Register, but the accused put a fake index number in the application for supplying the certified copy. From the application for supply of the certified copy of the disputed deed of gift Ext. 4 it is found that accused Mahfuzur Rahman wrote the applications and the learned Divisional Special Judge on careful consideration of the handwriting expert's opinion found that accused Mofizur Rahman is the author of these two applications. In the absence of any index against Ext. 4 accused Mofizur Rahman put an imaginary index number in the application for copy of the disputed deed of gift and from this the complicity of accused Mahfuzur Rahman in the offence is well established. The learned Divisional Special Judge on consideration of the material evidence on record, both oral and documentary, also found that the accused persons in collusion with each other have fraudulently made false entry in volume No. 11 of 1932 of the office of the Sub-Registrar, Bogra to give a colour of reality to Ext. 4 for facilitating a false claim for illegally grabbing the case property by accused Moyzuddin. The learned Divisional Special Judge, however, acquitted accused Aminur Rahman on benefit of doubt. Mr Gaziul Haque argues that in view of the fact that the certified copy of the disputed heba-bil-ewaj deed Ext. 4 was admittedly used in Title Suit No. 93 of 1986 before the Subordinate Judge, Bogra the present case except on the complaint of the learned Subordinate Judge, Bogra is not maintainable in law in view of the provision of section 195(c) of the Code of Criminal Procedure. For better appreciation of law on the subject we may profitably refer to the provision of section 195(1)(c) of the Code of Criminal Procedure which runs as follows: "Section 195(1) No Court shall take cognizance (e) of any offence described in section 463 punishable under section 471, section 475 or section 476 of the same Code. When such offence is alleged to have been committed by a party to any proceeding in any Court in respect of a document produced or given in evidence in such proceeding except on the complaint in writing of such Court, or of some other Court to which such Court is subordinate."

21. From a close scrutiny of the above provision of law it appears that section 195(1)(c) of the Code of Criminal Procedure has reference only to the forged document and it has no reference to a copy of it. The Court before which a copy of a false or forged document is produced is not really in a position to determine the genuineness or otherwise of the questioned deed as the original deed is not before it. The production of the certified copy of a forged document before a court does not, therefore, invoke the bar of a criminal prosecution under section 195(1)(c) of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

<u>22. The learned Assistant. Attorney-General, on the other hand, submits that the production of the certified copy of a forged deed before a Court is not protected by section 195(1) (c) of the Code of Criminal Procedure. In support of his contention he has placed reliance on the case of Sanmukhsing and another vs King reported in 3 DLR (PC). 3. In this case it has been held that section 195(1)(c) of the Code of Criminal Procedure has reference only to the forged document and not to a copy of it as from the production of a certified copy of a forged deed the Court is not in a position to express any opinion as to its genuineness or otherwise. I am in respectful agreement with the proposition of law enunciated in the cited decision. The submission made by the learned Advocate for the appellants on this score does not appear to have any substance and it is accordingly repelled. Consequently, I hold that section 195(1)(c) of the Code of Criminal Procedure has no manner of application in the facts and circumstances of the present case and, as such, it is not a bar against the prosecution of the accused appellants.</u>

23. The learned Advocate for the appellants submits that the learned Divisional Special Judge failed to consider the case of the individual accused persons in the light of the evidence on record. Mr Huq particularly lays emphasis on the case of accused Nuruddin Ahmed who was the Record Keeper of the Office of the Sub-Registrar Bogra. From a scrutiny of the evidence of record, I do not find any overt act that may be attributed to him for facilitating the creation of the disputed deed of gift of Ext 4. No doubt, he was the Record Keeper but from this it does not necessarily follow that others had no access to the records at any point of time. Moreover, it is never known as to when and under what circumstances the disputed deed of gift was created and entered into volume No. 11 of the year 1932. In the absence of any definite proof, it is highly unsafe to saddle him with a criminal liability, either director of abetment for the commission of the alleged offences.

24. In the facts and circumstances and the evidence on record, I find that accused appellant Nuruddin Ahmed is entitled to get the benefit of doubt. As regards the guilt of the other accused persons covered by both the appeals, I fully agree with the material findings of the learned Special Judge arrived at on due consideration and proper appreciation of the evidence on record. I am satisfied that the guilt of the accused appellants except accused appellant Nuruddin has been well proved by the most consistent and convincing evidence and consequently, I do not find any substance in their appeals. Accused, appellant Md Nuruddin Ahmed is thus found not guilty and he is acquitted of the charges levelled against him.

25. In the result, the appeals of accused appellant Md Hamidul Haque, Md Mahfuzur Rahman and Md Moyezuddin Akand are dismissed and the order of conviction and sentence passed against them by the learned Divisional Special Judge, Rajshahi Division is affirmed. The appeal of accused appellant Md Nuruddin is allowed and he is acquitted of the charges leveled against him.

26. Accused appellant Md Hamidul Haque, Md Mahfuzur Rahman and Md Moyezuddin Akand who are currently on bail, are directed to surrender immediately to their bail bonds to serve out the sentence imposed upon them. Accused appellant Md Nuruddin Ahmed, since acquitted, is discharged from his bail bond.

Send down the lower Court records at once.

End.
